title: Integral finite-Tor domains and coherent source comparisons for purity
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, with valuation rings and uniformizers [def-pur-conventions, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $W=X,Y$ put $R_{E,W}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $\mathbf1_{E,W}=R_{E,W}[0]$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the derived-complete integral constructible categories and their full uniform finite-Tor subcategories $\mathscr D_E(W)=D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with normalized reduction towers [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Write $L_E=Lf_E^*$, $P_E=Rf_{!,E}$, $G_E=Rf_E^!$, $T_E=\mathbf1_{E,X}(d)[2d]$ and $H_EK=L_EK(d)[2d]$, using completed pullback and tensor, the integral compact-support functor, its specified exceptional adjunction with counit $\epsilon_E$, and Tate twists [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Use exactness and linearity in [def-weil-triangulated-category, def-weil-linear-functor]. For $E\subset F$ put $C_{F/E,W}(M)=M\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{F,W}$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], identified with strict-tower extension by $\chi$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension, lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].
For nonnegative integer bounds $D_X,D_Y$ of the dimensions of $X,Y$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (use $0$ for an empty scheme), an input reduction Tor interval $[r,s]$ is carried by $P_E,G_E,H_E$ respectively into $[r,s+2D_X]$, $[r-2D_X,s+2D_Y]$, $[r-2d,s-2d]$. All three preserve derived-complete constructibility. The subcategories $\mathscr D_E(W)$ are triangulated, and $P_E\dashv G_E$ restricts to them. The functors $H_E,P_E$ are exact and $\mathcal O_E$-linear; $G_E$ and the exceptional Hom bijections are $\mathcal O_E$-linear. Equip $G_E$ with the counit-characterized adjunction shift comparison. The completed unit has reduction Tor interval $[0,0]$ and $T_E$ has interval $[-2d,-2d]$.
The exact functor $C_{F/E,W}$ preserves constructibility, completeness and the same common Tor interval, also for ramified extensions. The canonical pullback, tensor, twist and shift maps specify an exact natural source comparison
$$a_{F/E}:C_{F/E,X}H_E\xrightarrow{\sim}H_FC_{F/E,Y}.$$
With $\alpha^W_{L,F,E}:C_{L/F,W}C_{F/E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{L/E,W}$ the ordinary tensor associator, it satisfies
$$a_{L/E,K}\alpha^X_{L,F,E,H_EK}=H_L(\alpha^Y_{L,F,E,K})a_{L/F,C_{F/E,Y}K}C_{L/F,X}(a_{F/E,K}).$$
It is identity for $F=E$ under coefficient-unit identifications and commutes with the canonical shifts in $K$. At the unit its comparison is $q_{F/E}:C_{F/E,X}T_E\xrightarrow{\sim}T_F$ with the canonical coefficient-unit identifications. These comparisons use the ordinary tensor associators under $\chi$, not independently chosen tower identifications. The compact-support coefficient maps are the specified exact natural isomorphisms $c_{F/E}:C_{F/E,Y}P_E\xrightarrow{\sim}P_FC_{F/E,X}$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-integral-coefficient-comparison], with its unit, composition, projection, finite-reduction and shift normalizations.

source.place: Proof Steps 2-3; extracted argument of lem-pur-adic-purity-scalar-naturality, former Steps 1-5
source.note: Agent auxiliary argument on the diagonal-purity/reconstruction route; no Stacks tag states this completed integral compatibility.

proof.text: For $K\in\mathscr D_E(Y)$, the reduction formula for completed pullback identifies $(L_EK)_n$ with $f_n^*K_n$. Finite-stage pullback preserves constructibility and the interval $[r,s]$. Twisting by $(d)$ preserves that same interval and derived-complete constructibility. Finally $[2d]$ keeps the object in the integral finite-Tor constructible class, which is closed under shifts, and, since derived reduction commutes with shift, changes the reduction interval to $[r-2d,s-2d]$. These statements prove the asserted preservation and quantitative bound for $H_E$, with one interval independent of $n$.

source.place: Step 2, common bounds for the twisted inverse-image system

proof.text: Apply integral compact-support preservation with dimension bound $D_X$ and input interval $[r,s]$: it gives $P_EK\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with reduction interval $[r,s+2D_X]$. Apply the integral exceptional-adjoint theorem with bounds $D_X,D_Y$: it gives $G_EK\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ with interval $[r-2D_X,s+2D_Y]$, together with the specified adjunction and reduction counits. Both functors therefore preserve the uniform finite-Tor subcategories. Those are full triangulated subcategories by integral finite-Tor triangulated closure. Restricting the existing Hom bijections to these full subcategories gives $P_E\dashv G_E$ there. For an empty source or target use the stated bound $0$; no negative dimension is substituted.

source.place: Step 2 and Step 5, the integral constructible adjunction and its finite-Tor domain

proof.text: The schemes are Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0,1$, so its spectrum is Noetherian, and finite type preserves this property. The supplied dimension bounds make them finite-dimensional. Hence the natural ordinary-to-completed pullback comparison is an isomorphism on these constructible inputs. Ordinary derived ringed pullback is exact and preserves the central $\mathcal O_E$ scalars: the structural coefficient map preserves every constant scalar, since its finite quotient projections do so. Thus $L_E$ is exact and $\mathcal O_E$-linear. The twist line is locally free of rank one; its ordinary tensor is exact and linear, and agrees naturally with completed line tensor. Shift is linear on the integral constructible category. The composite $H_E=L_E(-)(d)[2d]$ is consequently exact and linear.

source.place: Step 2, exact linear source functor; ordinary pullback and line-tensor interpretation

proof.text: Choose the compactification used to define $P_E$. The reduction-tower theorem supplies the actual exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor $\mathcal T_f^c$, including quotient transitions and arbitrary input morphisms. Use the total-limit realization theorem to choose $P_E= L_Y\mathcal T_f^c$ on integral constructible objects and $P_E(u)=L_Y(\mathcal T_f^c(u))$ on maps. Its Roos triangle realizes precisely the defining compact-support system. This is the specified functorial realization, not an identification of arbitrary choices of derived limits. The total limit $L_Y$ is exact. Its underived functor is additive and linear because compatible families are closed under addition and scalar multiplication; K-injective total right derivation preserves that linearity. Thus $P_E$ is exact and $\mathcal O_E$-linear. Fix its shift to be $s_{P,K}=s_{L_Y,\mathcal T_f^cK}\circ L_Y(s_{\mathcal T,K})$: a triangle with third arrow $w$ has image third arrow $s_{P,K}P_E(w)$ by the realization theorem. Step 2 permits restriction to the full finite-Tor categories. The operation datum is the stated small pro-etale datum, with $\ell\ne p$ and $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$; $f$ and both schemes satisfy its separated finite-type hypotheses. No equality of derived morphisms is inferred from equality of individual evaluations.

source.place: Step 5, the separately derived proper/open compact-support composite and its integral realization

proof.text: The integral constructible categories, hence their full finite-Tor subcategories, are $\mathcal O_E$-linear. Apply the linear-right-adjoint lemma to the restricted adjunction of Step 2 and the exact linear $P_E$ of Step 4: $G_E$ is additive and linear. If $\eta,\epsilon$ are its specified unit and counit, the adjunction and its inverse are $h\mapsto G_E(h)\eta_M$ and $v\mapsto\epsilon_KP_E(v)$. Both formulas are additive and scalar-linear by linearity of the functors and bilinearity of composition. For each integer shift, give $G_E$ the unique adjunction-compatible shift structure supplied by adjunction shift compatibility; its counit equation characterizes it. In fact this structure is exact by the triangulated-right-adjoint theorem.

source.place: Step 5, the specified exceptional adjunction, central scalars and counit-normalized shifts

proof.text: Ordinary $C_{F/E,W}$ is exact derived change of rings. The completed coefficient sheaf $R_{F,W}$ is finite free over $R_{E,W}$, and the specified comparison $\chi$ identifies ordinary extension with strict-tower extension on complete inputs and proves derived completeness of the result. Integral scalar extension preserves bounded constructibility, so the same holds for $C$. Its identities and composition comparisons hereafter are ordinary tensor unitors and associators, transported by this specified $\chi$ when using tower notation.

source.place: Steps 2-3, ordinary completed-ring scalar extension versus the strict-tower presentation

proof.text: Let $e=e(F/E)$, $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $B_{en}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^{en}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_F$. These $B_{en}$ are finite free over $A_n$. Derived scalar associativity identifies the $en$-th reduction of $CM$ with $M_n\otimes^L_{A_n}B_{en}$. Finite-free scalar calculus preserves its Tor interval $[r,s]$. For an arbitrary $m\ge1$, choose $en\ge m$; the $m$-th reduction is $(CM)_{en}\otimes^L_{B_{en}}B_m$. For every degree-zero $B_m$-module $N$, its tensor with this object identifies, by scalar associativity, with $(CM)_{en}\otimes^L_{B_{en}}N$, so vanishes outside $[r,s]$. Thus every reduction has the same interval. This calculation uses the cofinal $en$ levels; it does not assume same-index quotient maps are flat.

source.place: Step 3, finite coefficient extension on the uniform finite-Tor domain, including ramification

proof.text:
Write $S_E=(-)(d)$ and let $\theta_{F/E}:C_XL_E\to L_FC_Y$ be the canonical scalar/pullback comparison, expressed through $\chi$. Let $\beta_{F/E,M}:C_XS_EM\to S_FC_XM$ be the line scalar comparison. If $s_C:C_X(N[2d])\to(C_XN)[2d]$ is the canonical scalar shift, define
$$a_{F/E,K}=S_F(\theta_{F/E,K})[2d]\circ\beta_{F/E,L_EK}[2d]\circ s_{C,S_EL_EK,2d}.$$
Every factor is an invertible natural map. The framework/PBC bridge (2), with $h=f$, identifies $\theta:C_XL_E\to L_FC_Y$ under $\pi,j$ with $p_f=(\widehat\delta_f)^{-1}=\Lambda(\delta_f)^{-1}\circ\kappa$, since $\delta_f$ runs $F^{\mathrm{ord}}_{f,F}C_Y\to C_XF^{\mathrm{ord}}_{f,E}$. We use this inverse direction, not $\widehat\delta_f$. Clause (4) identifies the coefficient associators with the ordinary tensor associators. Tensor transport uses the relabeling comparisons $\tau^J$ on both sides, exactly as inserted in clause (3). The twist comparison is likewise the specified ordinary balanced tensor map transported by $\chi$. Thus this defines exactly the pullback/tensor/twist/shift source comparison of the statement on the domains established above. On the full finite-Tor subcategories, lift each specified component using ObjectProperty.isoMk. The inherited morphisms make its naturality exactly source_naturality. If another natural isomorphism has the same included components, faithfulness of the full-subcategory inclusion gives equality componentwise, and natural-transformation and isomorphism extensionality give equality of the natural isomorphisms. This proves sourceFiniteComparison_existsUnique without making any new choices of component maps.

source.place: Step 3, explicit source comparison before taking the exceptional adjunction mate

proof.text:
Before applying $[2d]$, the source comparison is $S_F\theta_{F/E}\circ\beta_{F/E,L_E(-)}$. Expand its two successive-extension components. Naturality of $\beta_{L/F}$ with respect to $\theta_{F/E}$ exchanges the middle two factors. The twist coefficient cocycle then replaces the two $\beta$ factors by $\beta_{L/E}$ and the scalar associator; the pullback coefficient cocycle replaces the two $\theta$ factors by $\theta_{L/E}$ and the scalar associator. All remaining associators are precisely $\alpha^X$ and $L_L\alpha^Y$. Applying the canonical coherent shift gives
$$a_{L/E,K}\alpha^X_{L,F,E,H_EK}=H_L(\alpha^Y_{L,F,E,K})a_{L/F,C_{F/E,Y}K}C_{L/F,X}(a_{F/E,K}).$$
For repeated fields both $\theta$ and $\beta$ are their coefficient-unit maps; the same composite is identity after the tensor-unit identifications. This proves the cocycle and unit normalization for the specified $a$.

source.place: Step 3, successive coefficient extension; explicit pasting of pullback and twist cocycles

proof.text: The $\theta$ comparison commutes with the specified canonical input shifts by framework scalar/pullback shift compatibility. For $\beta$, use its displayed flat-term K-flat formula $(x\otimes l)\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes b)\otimes(l\otimes1)$: the line and the scalar factors have degree zero. Thus shifting the $x$ slot gives the same map, with no new permutation of positive-degree factors; the total tensor signed shift formulas supply the coherent reindexings. The final shift $[2d]$ commutes with an input shift using the canonical addition of integer shifts (the interchange sign $(-1)^{2dm}$ is $1$). The comparison $\chi$ commutes with these shifts as well. Hence $a_{F/E,K[m]}$ is $a_{F/E,K}[m]$ under the canonical shift comparisons for every integer $m$. Since the source and target functors are exact, this makes $a$ an exact natural isomorphism.

source.place: Steps 2-3, exactness and the canonical signed shift normalization of the source comparison

proof.text:
The completed units $\mathbf1_{E,W}$ and their twists are in the integral constructible finite-Tor categories; their intervals are $[0,0]$ and, after $(d)[2d]$, $[-2d,-2d]$. At $K=\mathbf1_{E,Y}$ identify $L_E\mathbf1_{E,Y}$ with $\mathbf1_{E,X}$. By framework/PBC bridge (2), as in Step 8, $\theta$ is the inverse of reflected ordinary pullback/tensor balancing $\delta_f$. On the flat degree-zero unit both sides of $\delta_f$ are identified with $R_{F,X}$ by the pullback unit comparisons and the coefficient-unit multiplications, and $\delta_f$ sends the generator $1$ to $1$; the completion comparisons are the tensor-unit maps there. Hence the scalar/pullback unit comparison is multiplication, so Step 8 becomes exactly the shifted line coefficient map
$$q_{F/E}=(u_{F/E}(d)\circ\beta_{F/E,\mathbf1_{E,X}})[2d]\circ s_{C,\mathbf1_{E,X}(d),2d}.$$
Here $u$ is coefficient-unit multiplication. This is the specified $q$, not an arbitrary identification of the two twisted objects; its tower normalization is the ordinary one under $\chi$. For the separate Lean unitDomains clause, apply shiftedTateUnitScalarCoherence with F=E and the identity coefficient embedding at (X,d) and (Y,0), and take the E-domain projection in each case. This reuses the already specified unit and line constructions, including when d=0 or the scheme is empty.

source.place: Steps 2-3, normalization on the coefficient unit and its shifted Tate twist

proof.text: Take $c_{F/E}$ to be exactly the compact-support integral coefficient comparison. Its theorem supplies the proper-then-open construction on cofinal finite-free quotient towers, the inverse isomorphism, independence of compactification, projection compatibility, quotient reductions, the unit and coefficient-composition equations and compatibility with canonical shifts. Steps 2, 4, 6 and 7 put both endpoints on the stated exact finite-Tor domains. Thus it is an exact natural isomorphism with all the required normalizations. This uses its actual tower construction, rather than an independently chosen family of finite reduction isomorphisms. In Lean the separate compactSupport_exact clause is precisely comparison_commShift for the published completedChange and the given compactification.
